summary: The III notes introduce fhr, fxr (< MEA phr ... to yawn), followed by II mfahər/(mifahər), Detransitive gähnen and Kfarze mfaxar. This is a separate root section accidentally attached to fhm.
rationale: Neither the consonants nor the yawning gloss belongs to fhm. Extract the fhr/fxr heading and following II section intact, preserving fhm.II.d.infectum.1 and fhm.II.d.infectum.2 as provenance; do not reinterpret these as fhm evidence.

summary: Separate the fhr/fxr yawning entry from fhm

data.head: fhr, fxr (< MEA phr cf. SL 1158: to yawn;)

rationale: The fhr/fxr entry heading is stored in fhm.III.notes, and its following mfahər/(mifahər) stem and two yawning examples are stored as fhm.II. The explicit heading and r-final forms identify a separate root, whereas fhm means understand. Restore the entry boundary and move the entire yawning stem with its notes and examples; do not change the informants' statements.

summary: File the -wa example mfaxarwayno under Infectum-wa
rationale: The example ends in mfaxarwayno, with the past -wa- plus first-person ending, and begins aṯmәl (yesterday). It is filed in the plain Infectum box beside k-mifaharno. Preserve the dialectal x and the personal-communication attribution; the required change is to the tense box.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (30/38)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d mḥalaqle iḏe lu šex lab buġre, aḏəʕ — meqəm de lo məštaʕanwo ʕam ḥḏoḏe meqəm? — aḏəʕ i garre d iḏe, kəfhəmle, ʕAbdallalməṭṭaləb yo, w lə mtanele u paša.
data.translation: Als der Scheich dies Pielsteine faßte, da erkannte jener - hatten sie nicht schon früher miteinander gespielt? - da erkannte er das Kreisen seiner Band und merkte, daß es ʕAbdalmuttalib war. Er sagte aber nichts, der Pascha.

rationale: New ko-Preterit box: kəfhəmle has the L-suffixed Preterit shape, unlike Infectum kfohəm.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.I/299)

data.turoyo: ʕAṭiya Xamri: Hənnək xəd u mede d mašmaʕlox karye ne, bas kətte ġalabe maʕna d ašan d məfhomi.
data.translation: Atiya Khamri: Those, like what you have let us hear, are short, but they have much meaning, for them to be understood.

rationale: First Detransitive Infectum/1 with the short meaningful texts as referent; one attestation, without deriving the analysis from English.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.39/1750)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Afandəm ənkan mərlan l aḥna, i naqqayo əmminawo mafhəminawo ar rayyəs ǧəmhurin stene, əno ǧġəlno ʕam ar rayyəs ǧəmhurin stene w ǧġəlno ʕam riše daw wazire stene ġalabe, mərlilən, <...>
data.translation: Uncle Isho: Sir, if we had spoken, at that time we used to say it, explain it even to the presidents of the republic. I spoke with presidents of the republic too, and spoke with prime ministers too, a great deal. I told them. <...>

rationale: First III Infectum-wa; overt recipient presidents contrasts with previously documented suffix recipients.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.5/1638)

data.turoyo: Umarno: "Alo, əno stene kətlilox raǧa, yaʕni šəwolo." Omər: "Abuna, ʕal aʕ ʕayne, mar! D huwela əmkan!" Umarno: "I maqbarayo, d kətyo si ʕitayḏan flan, flan..." Mafhamlile.
data.translation: I say, 'Well, I too have a request of you, that is, a business matter.' He says, 'Father, gladly, say it! If it is possible!' I say, 'That cemetery which is beside our church, so-and-so, so-and-so...' I explained it to him.

rationale: First secure III Preterit after round 1: preceding request supplies the cemetery topic and recipient.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) verstanden werden
rationale: Purpose clause d ašan d məfhomi has the meaningful short texts as affected participants. One explicit m-form attestation; no agent is named.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/12)

data.turoyo: i barṯo madʕalla, fhəmto wa ġalabe.
data.translation: Die Tochter antwortete, denn sie war sehr klug.
data.ref: Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/12

rationale: Thin Part act. cell: feminine dispositional predicate with wa, matching inherited fahəmto.

evidence.cite: Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/12

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 3.2/12)

data.turoyo: Aṣ ṣuroye fəhmiwo ʕal i ləġaṯe dəṯṯe.
data.translation: Die Christen verstanden ihre Sprache.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: overt ʕal-marked language stimulus, contrasting with inherited b- and m- contexts.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (MAC Hanna Dewo/79)

data.turoyo: Košəmʕat? Fahimat u+xabrano?
data.translation: Have you heard? Did you understand this word?

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive cell: fahimat with overt zero-marked definite u+xabrano; decisive nominal-stimulus evidence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (MAC Ishaq Material culture/90)

data.turoyo: Fahimina haṯe, tawdi ġắlabe, kə́tlilŭx šŭwolo, tre+ḥrene.
data.translation: (Now) we understand this, thanks a lot, I have a question for you, two more.

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive cell: 1pl result-state with zero-marked demonstrative haṯe; keep distinct from a lexical noun.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (29/289)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Ksamno raǧa m aloho w menux, d obatli ḥa malfono, fahomo du kṯowo.
data.translation: "Ich bitte dich um Gottes willen, daß du mir einen Lehrer gibst, der sich aufs schriftliche versteht.

rationale: Thin Part act. cell: attributive fahomo with d-marked literacy domain; retain printed form.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (45/25)

data.turoyo: Haṯe simole lu Qanda, ḥatta d lo foyəš noše fohəmtər mene bi qriṯayo.
data.translation: Das tat Qanda aber, damit niemand im Dorfe bleiben sollte, der klüger wäre als er.

rationale: Thin Part act. cell and unusual comparative -tər of the understanding adjective; not a finite person suffix.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (52/135)

data.turoyo: Fohumto wa. Ḥəlla, məlla: "Hn! Hat abre d ʕammi hat! Li šittayo hawxa səmla ebux, lo?"
data.translation: Sie war klug. Sie schaute und sprach: Hallo! Bist du mein Vetter? Hat dir das die Teufelin angetan?

rationale: Thin Part act. cell: source Fohumto with wa adds a vocalic variant; lexical status remains an editorial question.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (54/59)

data.turoyo: U muxtar fhəmle i masale omər: "Ṭayyəb, uʕdo l mən aṯutu l gabi?"
data.translation: Der Schultheiß verstand, was gespielt wurde, und sprach: "Schön! Und warum seid ihr jetzt zu mir gekommen?"

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: overt definite i masale with L-suffixed experiencer, for comparison with qaṭəl nominal stimuli.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (59/89)

data.turoyo: U zʕuro fohamwo i ǧġaliye du qarqurano w goḥaxwo.
data.translation: Der Junge verstand, was das Lamm sagte, und lachte dann immer.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: nominal speech stimulus and recurring comprehension.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (83/7)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d ḥəzyole, rafi w lo kofohamwo mede.
data.translation: Als er sie sah, versagten ihm die Kräfte und er verstand gar nichts (mehr).

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: overt indefinite mede under negation, with ko- and -wo.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (93/43)

data.turoyo: Faqat ono ʕal u=mede, d ḥəlli eba, naqqa=ḥreto lə=kšəbho laḥ=ḥarfat d latin, innu kṯawto b u=šəkəl d ab=basmore yo. W lo=fahəmno mede mina.
data.translation: Nach dem, was ich davon angesehen habe, gleichen die Buchstaben jedoch nicht den lateinischen; es ist eine Schrift in Form von Nägeln. Ich habe nichts davon Verstanden.

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive cell: 1sg negative mede plus m-partitive, comparable with L-suffixed 93/39.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (95/138)

data.turoyo: Omər: “Kali komannolax”, — omər, — “ono Ḥasane Aliki, qum!” Maquyole ġalabe, axər fhəmla, d kətyo Ḥasane Aliki.
data.translation: Aber ich sage dir doch, ich bin Ḥasan Aliki! Steh auf! - Er redete so lange auf sie ein, bis sie endlich begriff, daß er Ḥasan Aliki war.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell and unusual feminine -la experiencer with d-clausal stimulus.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 5.5/5)

data.turoyo: omər kubaʕno d mafhəmatli mede ʕal u zʕurano, d əmmatli u ədrakayḏe yaʕni b mə šəkəl latyo qawyo?
data.translation: Er sagte: Ich möchte, dass du mir etwas über diesen Jungen erklärst, dass du mir sagst, in welcher Hinsicht seine Auffassungsgabe nicht besonders stark ist.

rationale: Thin III Infectum cell: overt mede content, ʕal topic and recipient -li together.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq Material culture/94)

data.turoyo: Maḥtiwa niro ʕal qarʕe da+tre, hánəkste ṭabi balki, ḥa dlowe bi+ṣərto, ḥa lə+qodar mafhamle.
data.translation: They put the yoke on the head of the two, so those ones naturally, maybe, if one isn’t in the picture (Fig. 1), one cannot explain it.

rationale: Thin III Infectum cell: mafhamle under qdr has a thing-object suffix, despite resembling the citation Preterit.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Famine/69)

data.turoyo: Hăma háyoste gmafəhmallux, d̥šaḥino mi+adro doṯe, gnəflo i+qalmo ebe.
data.translation: But I’ll explain to you this too, when it comes hot off the threshing floor, lice fall into it.

rationale: Thin III Infectum cell: explicit content and recipient in a prospective explanation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 4.I/558)

data.turoyo: ʕAṭiya Xamri: Šəbqono ḥabro Ǧan u zabnayḏan karyo yo, fahəmina i məlṯayḏox. <...>
data.translation: Atiya Khamri: Excuse me, our friend Jan, our time is short; we have understood your word. <...>

rationale: Selected beyond the round-1 five-example count for research value: clear lexical nominal stimulus i məlṯayḏox with 1pl Preterit Intransitive.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (Jan 2.10/2310)

data.turoyo: <...> Omər: "Əlla gdəzzan sə ḥawroni! Mafhəmme u medano!"
data.translation: <...> He says: "You must go to my friends! Explain the matter to them!"

rationale: III Imperativ remains thin: recipient suffix -me with overt u medano content.

summary: L-suffixed Preterit fhəmle/fhəmli alternates with Preterit Intransitive fahəm, fahimat, fahimina and fahəmno. Clausal, elliptical and nominal stimuli must be distinguished: MAC Hanna Dewo/79 has the clear lexical NP u+xabrano with fahimat; MAC Ishaq Material culture/90 has demonstrative haṯe; 26/57 and 93/43 have negative mede plus m-partitive. These do not support an unrestricted ban on nominal stimuli in the latter box.

Present comprehension checks occur with both Preterit Intransitive and ko-Infectum, including adjacent fahimat? Kofəhmat? in Lahdo Traitor 2/28. A current result reading is not grounds to relabel the box Infectum. Isolated fahəmno can also resemble a participial predicate, so morphology and context remain relevant.

The m- phrase is not a reliable diagnostic of memorising: 1/20 and 93/48 concern expertise, JL 8.11/11 has reciprocal understanding, and MAC NE interview 1/25 permits priests as source or stories as content. Keep the inherited native memorise gloss without projecting it onto every m- token.

III retains explaining with recipient l-suffixes and optional overt content; MAC Ishaq Material culture/94 illustrates a thing-object suffix after qdr. MAC Hanna Dewo/109 describes places without changing the basic sense.

Part act. includes inherited dispositional fahəmto. The new comparative fohəmtər and Fohumto are filed alongside it provisionally; fahomo, fohumo and fohume need morphological comparison rather than being treated as qaṭəl experiencer forms.
No light-verb collocation is demonstrated; Arabic origin and general contact tags alone do not establish one.

Preterit Intransitive remains distinct from Infectum despite frequent current-understanding/discourse-check uses. Jan 4.I/558 fahəmina i məlṯayḏox gives a lexical nominal stimulus; Jan 2.16/3563 Fahimət mede is an indefinite stimulus; Jan 1.21/1076 and 1.31/1379 contain relative gaps, not equally direct lexical NP evidence.
The many fahimat comprehension checks in Jan 4.II repeat a discourse pattern already exemplified in round 1. They receive individual decisions but no repeated thin-cell additions.
Infectum contrasts ʕal-pronominal stimuli (Jan 4.II/1021) with personal suffix -nne and content suffix -le (1023). min with expertise in law or medicine does not mean memorise by itself.

Round-1 structural extraction of the accidentally attached fhr/fxr yawning material is retained; no duplicate correction is proposed. The human entry omits that foreign-root stem II section after applying the round-1 extraction.

Jan fəhman is an adjectival/dispositional formation and may reflect borrowed Arabic morphology. Round 1 already fills Part act.; a new stem or an independent intelligence sense would outrun this evidence.

Six compact records lack full verses. Their reader labels are retained only provisionally in decisions, with rejected_analysis indicating that independent verification was impossible. No quotations or positive corpus claims are based on them.
Check 93/25 fhim against the edition or a speaker: Detransitive Preterit, an impersonal active use, or spelling variant? No Detransitive form or sense is proposed until resolved.

The supplied translation at 111/107 is flagged mismatched; check the edition and whether mə fhəmwaylux mena means understanding/learning or lexically obtaining benefit. The inherited literal German example remains unchanged.
The supplied translation at 115/184 is flagged partial; verify the exact verse boundary before adding it.
Recover the omitted verse and edition translation for compact 65/231; its analysis could not be checked.
Are fahomo, fohumo, fohume, Fohumto and comparative fohəmtər productive Part act. variants or lexical adjectives? Is 1sg fahəmno always Preterit Intransitive in these acknowledgment contexts?
Does initial Qaḥfure in MAC NE Interview 2/147 have direct-object prosody or a detached quotation/topic? Is be in MAC MuA Quzko/56 a question/complement marker?
Confirm the extraction boundary of the inherited fhr/fxr yawning section and the status of -at endings in the MAC narrators before inferring gender.

Check the original Turoyo for the six compact records before treating their analyses as verified: Jan 4.II/640 fəhmono, Jan 4.II/653 fəhmina, Jan 4.II/727 kfəhmono, Jan 4.II/747 kfohəm, Jan 4.II/822 fohəm, Jan 4.II/946 fohəm.
Jan 2.25/4346 lawi darbo b mafhamli and 2.31/5111 mafhamli: resolve contracted III Preterit/Infectum versus ma + fhəmli. Neither ambiguous token establishes a new box.
Jan 2.17/3641 fəhmatwole: confirm Infectum-wa versus Preterit Intransitive plus -wo and how -le indexes Eastern Syriac.
Jan 2.35/5661: is fəhman a borrowed adjective or productive Part act. formation? Keep the source form.
Jan 4.II/900: identify the experiencer of fragmentary lə kfəhmo; a third feminine interpretation after a first-person statement is not secure.
Jan 1.44/1890: confirm person of quoted Kfəhmi before using it as a person-specific paradigm example.
Repair the misspelling Kaufman=ns → Kaufmanns
rationale: The German genitive is Kaufmanns; the supplied edition translation of 23/47 has Kaufmanns. The internal equals sign is a typo in the German word.

summary: Understanding extends to dream interpretation, coded language, animal calls and expertise in valuable objects; these are participant/domain specialisations of existing understanding, not separate senses.
Explanation includes describing concrete villages and material processes; this changes the content, not the explaining construction.
Expertise in weather, law, medicine and old books continues the round-1 domain extension of understanding. min marks domain/source here; none of these passages independently establishes memorising.
Explaining one's situation to authorities (including zero-marked ar rayyəs ǧəmhurin) retains III.1, rather than a separate reporting sense.
